observations.statement: Remaining local weights give compact-open Schwartz support, fixed character ring and global even scaling character via root-sign formula. Finite unit groups inject modulo3, so c0 clears automorphism denominators integrally without theta precision loss.

Weil operators with self-dual measures give upper and sufficiently deep lower unipotent invariance from Fourier support. Dyadic reference lattice dual is half-lattice with factor2^-3/2; no false self-duality at2 is used.

Quaternion norm Weil-index identities give the ternary determinant character. Explicit Fourier/Bruhat relations construct a common double cover with form-independent scalars and retain order4 lift of -I at2. Eigenvalue quotient is lift-independent.

Comparison to literal theta³ fixes dyadic root-of-unity normalization. Triangular decomposition treats every prescribed-prime matrix; inverse finite adelic action gives lower-right classical character. Hilbert reciprocity retains the dyadic factor and yields eta_B(m/d), with quotient chi_-1.

Outside support, self-dual split lattice is spherical. Global Weil invariance plus positive-definite lattice-coset expansions proves cusp holomorphy. Replacing Q by Q/m extracts exact coefficients with no Haar measure or degree factor; character changes by squareclass m only.

All-index Hecke recurrence counts integral invariant lines and unique nonintegral neighbor, including nilpotent/divisible cases. Dual-isogeny mass symmetry moves operator onto actual P_M; scaling phases yield both eta powers. Added sieves preserve recurrence only outside enlarged support.

Weighted comparison requires maximal CM order, fixed good-model specialization and separate enhanced supersingular correspondence. Local embedding classification gives2^(omegaN+1) orientations including2; centralizer and adelic quotient give actual Pic torsor, not an averaged orbit.

Genus character compatibility uses discriminant equality for the biquadratic extension, hence unramified restriction to F, and full class-field norm compatibility. D=1 is trivial; quadratic inversion convention leaves result unchanged.

Conductor-one reduction is equivariant bijection onto the fixed-type orientation, not both residue signs. Same place and same additive lambda give unaveraged finite-sum identity; weights are constant on order-unit orbits and Pic torsor up to genus character.

Stabilizer ±1 yields exactly half mass per embedding orbit; x and -x are different residue orientations. Fixed-character phase does not grow with D or precision. Level normalizers require actual geometric Atkin action and cusp annihilator, canceling Schwartz and norm signs; division orientation is treated separately.
